title: NHS Fraudster Tanya Nasir Ordered to Repay Just £278
excerpt: A UK court orders token repayment after nurse faked her way into a neonatal ward, pocketing over £51,000 in fraudulent NHS wages.
body:
A Cardiff Crown Court ordered Tanya Nasir — jailed in 2024 for faking her nursing qualifications — to repay just £278.13 of the £51,397.58 she fraudulently earned from the NHS. The ruling came on May 7, 2025, after the court heard she was living on benefits and was nearly penniless.

**What Nasir did:**
Nasir, 47, managed a unit caring for premature babies at Bridgend's Princess of Wales Hospital for five months before being found out. She fabricated qualifications, listed universities she never attended, and falsely claimed she had been shot twice while deployed overseas in the military — a claim investigators at the NHS Local Counter Fraud Authority flatly disproved. Cardiff Crown Court found her guilty on nine counts of fraud and false representation and sentenced her to five years in prison in October 2024.

**Why the repayment is so small:**
The court calculated that Nasir earned the fraudulent sum by claiming to be a Band 7 senior nurse when she was only qualified for Band 5. But with just £278.13 sitting in her bank account, that is all the court could order her to pay — split between £13.91 to Hillingdon NHS Trust and £264.22 to Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board. Fraud investigators told the court they will pursue Nasir if she comes into money in the future.

**What to watch next:**
The Nursing and Midwifery Council has already struck Nasir off its register, and the question of whether NHS trusts can recover more meaningful sums under the Proceeds of Crime Act remains open if her financial circumstances change.

nri_angle: For Indian-American healthcare professionals who navigate rigorous credential verification to practise in the US, this case is a sharp reminder of how credential fraud endangers patients and erodes the hard-won trust that legitimate immigrant nurses and doctors depend on.
